title: Edmund and the Witness
premise: Jude Underhill, a night-shift dispatcher who has catalogued a decade of the city's tragedies from behind a radio console, is handed the diary of Marisol Vega, a missing woman whose entries keep being written after her disappearance — in handwriting that isn't hers. Following the diary's clues through taxi logs, abandoned depots, and the city's forgotten hours, Jude discovers that Marisol faked her death to escape a powerful man, and that the 'dead witness' everyone mentions is Marisol herself. When the man hunting her closes in, Jude must choose between reporting what she knows and protecting the woman she has come to love; in the end she helps Marisol vanish for real, sacrificing her own clean record and her sense of duty to give someone else a new identity.
about_author: Isandro Yarrow is the pen name of a former emergency-services dispatcher who spent seven years working the overnight shift before turning to fiction. They write mysteries set in the small hours, where cities tell their truest stories.

chapters.title: The Last Fare Logged
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. On a slow night shift, Jude takes custody of Marisol Vega's recovered diary from a detective friend, expecting closure for a cold case. Instead, the final entry is dated three days after Marisol vanished — and describes a taxi ride Jude herself dispatched. The beat is quiet dread: the case Jude thought was over has just opened its eyes.

chapters.title: Entries That Outlive Their Author
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Jude cross-references the impossible entries against dispatch archives and finds the rides are real — fares picked up by a cab that was scrapped years ago. Her detective friend warns her off; the file belongs to people with more power than badges. Emotional beat: obsession taking root, the thrill of a puzzle no one wants solved.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Back Seat
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jude and diary excerpts. A late-night fare turns out to be Marisol, alive, disguised, terrified — she slips Jude a note before vanishing at a depot gate. The diary, Jude realizes, is being planted as breadcrumbs. Beat: vertigo and wonder; the dead woman is writing to whoever is clever enough to read.

chapters.title: What the Depot Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Digging into the decommissioned cab's history, Jude learns Marisol witnessed a hit-and-run cover-up involving city councilman Aldous Renner, and that the 'witness' officially died in a fire meant to erase her. Beat: fear arrives — Jude finds her own name on a list of people asking too many questions.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Duty
chapters.summary: POV: Jude with flashbacks to her dispatcher years. Jude's mentor pressures her to hand over the diary, framing silence as loyalty and disclosure as betrayal of the force that raised her. A second planted entry leads her to a safehouse address. Beat: torn between institutional belonging and a stranger's survival.

chapters.title: The Address on Ash Street
chapters.summary: POV: Jude and Marisol. Jude finds Marisol hiding above a shuttered laundromat; over one long night they trade histories — Marisol's erased life, Jude's loneliness behind the headset. Something tender and unspoken forms between them. Beat: intimacy blooming in a place built for hiding.

chapters.title: Renner's People
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Marisol ventures out to retrieve evidence hidden before her 'death' and realizes Renner's fixer has been following the diary's trail too — using it to hunt her. She barely escapes, and the safehouse is burned. Beat: the breadcrumb trail has become a leash, and both women are caught on it.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Jude confronts her detective friend and learns he's been feeding Renner's office information under duress; his guilt gives her the location of the original crash evidence. She must decide whether to trust him or go alone. Beat: betrayal, forgiveness, and the cold clarity of commitment.

chapters.title: Terminal Hour
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jude and Marisol. At the impound yard where the wrecked cab and the evidence ledger sit, Renner's fixer springs his trap. Jude uses her dispatcher skills to orchestrate a fleet-wide radio misdirection that strands the fixer, while Marisol secures the ledger. Climax: love against duty, enacted in real time.

chapters.title: A New Name, an Open Road
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. With the ledger delivered anonymously and Renner under investigation, Jude forges one last fare record — a ride out of the city for a passenger who officially never existed. She stays behind, changed, keeping the diary's final blank pages. Resolution: belonging redefined; some witnesses live so others can testify.
